# Add a boot node (or prove you should not)

Full recipe: **`docs/framework/recipes/add-boot-node.md`**.

## 0. The gate before you write anything

> **Boot node ⟺ it must be _awaited_, OR it can _fail meaningfully_, OR it needs _external
> ordering_.** None of the three → it is **not** a boot node.

| Answer | Tier | Write |
|---|---|---|
| None of the three | **1** | A constructor. The container builds it. |
| It is **feature** startup (mission, shop refresh, match setup) | **3** | `IAsyncStartable` in the feature's own child scope |
| One of the three holds, and it is framework/app-wide | **2** | `IBootNode` — continue below |

**A feature-init node in the kernel is a boundary violation** — the kernel must not know your game
features exist. **Adding a kernel boot node is a spine change** — route it. A tier-3 feature startup
in your own scope is not, and needs no routing.

## 1. Capabilities, never node names

```csharp
public string Id => "ShopCatalog";
public IReadOnlyList<BootCap> Requires => new[] { BootCaps.ConfigAvailable, BootCaps.UserDataLoaded };
public IReadOnlyList<BootCap> Provides => new[] { GameBootCaps.ShopCatalogReady };
```

Framework caps: `LoggingReady` · `ConfigAvailable` · `UserDataLoaded` · `LocalizationReady` ·
`AssetReady` · `UiReady` · `ConsentResolved` · `ClockSynced` · `RemoteConfigFresh` · `AdsReady` ·
`IapReady` · `AnalyticsReady`.

## 2. The race rule — the whole point

> **A node ctor-injects only services whose readiness is asserted by its `Requires` caps.**

Need `IGameConfig`? Then you must require `ConfigAvailable`. No exceptions, and no "it happens to
work". This is rule #5 and it is the race the graph exists to prevent.

## 3. The rest of the surface

| Member | Choose |
|---|---|
| `Required` | `true` ⇒ failure aborts boot + error screen. `false` ⇒ logged, boot continues. Default `false` unless the game is genuinely unplayable without it. |
| `SoftTimeout` | Elapsed ⇒ `Degraded`, **and the task keeps running** — a late arrival is still usable. |
| `HardTimeout` | Elapsed ⇒ the task is actually cancelled. |
| `Predicate` | `false` ⇒ `Skipped`, and it **still emits `Provides`** — dependents are not stranded. |
| `ExclusiveGroup` | Same non-empty group ⇒ serialized. |
| `Weight` | Relative cost, **never a duration**. Only the `Framework/Boot Graph` preview reads it. |

## 4. Threading is yours

The framework never moves your node off-thread (rule #6):

```csharp
await UniTask.RunOnThreadPool(() => ParseTheBigCatalog(), cancellationToken: ct);
```

## 5. Gate

`Framework/Boot Graph` previews the schedule. `BootGraph.Validate()` rejects missing/cyclic
capabilities and runs under `TestCategory=DataValidation`; `Framework/Doctor` check 7 runs it too.
The authoritative gate is the Unity `-runTests` step plus an actual runtime boot — the real node
list is DI-assembled. Locally that boot is the earned **boot smoke** (one boot, `pf-gates`), never the
PlayMode suite.

## If it breaks

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| A service is null / half-built in `RunAsync` | Race rule broken — you injected something `Requires` does not assert. |
| Boot hangs | A node awaits forever with no `HardTimeout`. |
| Boot aborts on something non-essential | `Required` is `true` where it should be `false`. |
| A dependent is stranded when a node is skipped | The cap is missing from `Provides` — `Skipped` still emits them. |
| Nothing renders while booting | Expected. The boot cover is **SKU-owned**. |
